\[
c_{j,b} = \mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(M_{j,b}\, \mathcal{F} I\big),
\quad
M_{j,b}(r, \theta) = L(r) \prod_{i<j} L(2^{i+1} r)\, H(2^{j+1} r)\, G_b(\theta),
\qquad
G_b(\theta) = \alpha_K \cos^K\!\big(\theta - \tfrac{\pi b}{K+1}\big),
\qquad
\hat{I} = \sum_{j,b} \mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\overline{M_{j,b}}\, \mathcal{F}\,\eta_{T_{j,b}}(c_{j,b})\big) + \ldots,
\quad
T_{j,b} = k\, \sigma\, \lVert a_{j,b} \rVert,
\qquad
K + 1 = \text{4},\ J = 4,\ k = 3
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(c_{j,b}\): The coefficients of band b at level j
- \(M_{j,b}\): The whole frequency mask of band b at level j
- \(H, L\): The radial high-pass and low-pass masks, a raised cosine one octave wide
- \(G_b\): The angular mask of band b
- \(K\): The order of the angular masks, one less than the number of orientations
- \(\alpha_K\): The scale that makes the squares of the angular masks add up to 1
- \(\lVert a_{j,b} \rVert\): The norm of the filter of band b at level j
- \(k\): The threshold factor
- \(\eta_T\): The shrink rule with threshold T

The steerable pyramid splits the spectrum of an image into rings an octave wide. Each ring is split into K + 1 smooth wedges of direction. r is the frequency radius, 1 at the Nyquist frequency, and theta its angle. H(r) = cos(pi/2 log2 r) rises from 0 at r = 1/2 to 1 at r = 1. L(r) is the square root of 1 - H(r)^2, so the squares of H and L add up to 1. Levels are counted from j = 0, the finest. Level j uses H and L with the radius doubled j + 1 times. After each level, the spectrum is cropped to half its size. The angular masks G_b are cos^K of the angle from the band's direction. alpha_K scales them so that their squares add up to 1. So the masks rebuild the image: filter each band once more with its own mask, and add up the results. The dots stand for the high-pass residual H(r) and the low-pass residual. The angular masks are cos^K, so a band at any angle is a fixed mix of the K + 1 bands. Freeman and Adelson called such filters steerable. To remove noise, each band coefficient c_j,b is shrunk with the rule eta and the threshold T_j,b. White noise of standard deviation sigma gives each band a noise level of sigma times the norm of its filter a_j,b. The filter measures that norm from the pyramid of a single bright pixel.
